entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13104"/><div sID="gen24642" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13104"/>4. So tranquil and prosperous shall the nation be that wars shall no longer prematurely cut off the people: men and women shall reach advanced ages. The promise of long life was esteemed one of the greatest blessings in the Jewish theocracy with its temporal rewards of obedience (<reference osisRef="Exod.20.12">Ex 20:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.4.40">De 4:40</reference>). Hence this is a leading feature in millennial blessedness (<reference osisRef="Isa.65.20">Is 65:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.65.22">22</reference>).<div eID="gen24642" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24643" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for very age--</hi>literally, "for multitude of days." <div eID="gen24643" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13106"/><div sID="gen24645" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13106"/>6. However impossible these things just promised by Me seem to you, they are not so with God. The "remnant" that had returned from the captivity, beholding the city desolate and the walls and houses in ruins, could hardly believe what God promised. The expression "remnant" glances at their ingratitude in rating so low God's power, though they had experienced it so "marvellously" displayed in their restoration. A great source of unbelief is, men "limit" God's power by their own (<reference osisRef="Ps.78.19">Psa 78:19</reference>, 20, 41).<div eID="gen24645" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24646" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">these days--</hi>"of small things" (<reference osisRef="Zech.4.10">Zec 4:10</reference>), when such great things promised seemed incredible. Maurer, after Jerome, translates, "in those days"; that is, if the thing which I promised to do in those days, seems "marvellous," &c. <div eID="gen24646" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13107"/><div sID="gen24647" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13107"/><hi type="bold">7. save my people from ... east ... west--</hi>that is, from every region (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.50.1">Psa 50:1</reference>; the "West" is literally, "the going down of the sun") to which they are scattered; they are now found especially in countries west of Jerusalem. The dispersion under Nebuchadnezzar was only to the east, namely, to Babylonia. The restoration, including a spiritual return to God (<reference osisRef="Zech.8.8">Zec 8:8</reference>), here foretold, must therefore be still future (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.11">Is 11:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.12">12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.43.5">43:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.43.6">6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.21">Eze 37:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.9.14">Am 9:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Amos.9.15">15</reference>; also <reference osisRef="Zech.13.9">Zec 13:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.30.22">Jr 30:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.1">31:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.31.33">33</reference>). <div eID="gen24647" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. save my people from ... east ... west-- that is, from every region (compare Psa 50:1 ; the "West" is literally, "the going down of the sun") to which they are scattered; they are now found especially in countries west of Jerusalem. The dispersion under Nebuchadnezzar was only to the east, namely, to Babylonia. The restoration, including a spiritual return to God ( Zec 8:8 ), here foretold, must therefore be still future ( Is 11:11 , 12 ; 43:5 , 6 ; Eze 37:21 ; Am 9:14 , 15 ; also Zec 13:9 ; Jr 30:22 ; 31:1 , 33 ).

All adversities formerly attended them when neglecting to build the temple: but now God promises all blessings, as an encouragement to energy in the work.<div eID="gen24649" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24650" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hands ... strong--</hi>be of courageous mind (<reference osisRef="2Sam.16.21">2Sa 16:21</reference>), not merely in building, but in general, as having such bright prospects (<reference osisRef="Zech.8.13">Zec 8:13</reference>, &c.).<div eID="gen24650" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24651" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">these days--</hi>the time that had elapsed between the prophet's having spoken "these words" and the time (<reference osisRef="Zech.8.10">Zec 8:10</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Hag.2.15-Hag.2.19">Hag 2:15-19</reference>) when they set about in earnest restoring the temple.<div eID="gen24651" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24652" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the prophets--</hi>Haggai and Zechariah himself (<reference osisRef="Ezra.5.1">Ezr 5:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.2">2</reference>). I thought--</hi>I determined.<div eID="gen24662" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24663" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">you--</hi>that is, your fathers, with whom ye are one; the Jewish Church of all ages being regarded as an organic whole (compare <reference osisRef="Hag.2.5">Hag 2:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.23.31">Mt 23:31</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.23.32">32</reference>).<div eID="gen24663" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24664" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">repented not--</hi>I changed not My purpose, because they changed not their mind (<reference osisRef="2Chr.36.16">2Ch 36:16</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13117"/><div sID="gen24670" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13117"/>18-19. The prophet answers the query (<reference osisRef="Zech.7.3">Zec 7:3</reference>) as to the fast in the fifth month, by a reply applying to all their fasts: these are to be turned into days of rejoicing. So Jesus replied to His disciples when similarly consulting Him as to why fasting was not imposed by Him, as it was by John the Baptist. When the Sun of righteousness shines, tears are dried up (<reference osisRef="Matt.9.15">Mt 9:15</reference>). So hereafter (<reference osisRef="Isa.35.10">Is 35:10</reference>). <div eID="gen24670" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13119"/><div sID="gen24675" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13119"/>20. (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.3">Is 2:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.4.2">Mi 4:2</reference>).<div eID="gen24675" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24676" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Thus saith the Lord of hosts--</hi>a preface needed to assure the Jews, now disheartened by the perils surrounding them, and by the humble aspect of the temple. "Unlikely as what follows may seem to you, Jehovah of hosts, boundless in resources, saith it, therefore it shall be so." Just before Christ's coming, a feeling grew up among the heathen of the unsatisfactoriness of their systems of religion and philosophy; this disposed them favorably towards the religion of the Jew, so that proselytes embraced the worship of Jehovah from various parts of Asia; these again were predisposed to embrace Christianity when it was preached to them (Ac 2:9-12, 41). But the full accomplishment of the conversion of the Gentiles foretold here is reserved till "Jerusalem" (<reference osisRef="Zech.8.22">Zec 8:22</reference>) becomes the center of Christianized Jewry (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.12">Ro 11:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.15">15</reference>). <div eID="gen24676" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13120"/><div sID="gen24677" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13120"/><hi type="bold">21. Let us ... I--</hi>manifesting zeal and love: converted themselves, they seek the conversion of others (<reference osisRef="Song.1.4">So 1:4</reference>). To exhortation in general ("Let us go"), they add individual example ("I will go"). Or, the change from plural to singular implies that the general consent in religious earnestness leads each individual to decide for God.<div eID="gen24677" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24678" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">go speedily--</hi>literally, "go, going"; implying intense earnestness.<div eID="gen24678" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24679" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">pray--</hi>Hebrew, "entreat the face" (<reference osisRef="Zech.7.2">Zec 7:2</reference>); entreat His favor and grace. <div eID="gen24679" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 21. Let us ... I-- manifesting zeal and love: converted themselves, they seek the conversion of others ( So 1:4 ). To exhortation in general ("Let us go"), they add individual example ("I will go"). Or, the change from plural to singular implies that the general consent in religious earnestness leads each individual to decide for God. go speedily-- literally, "go, going"; implying intense earnestness. pray-- Hebrew, "entreat the face" ( Zec 7:2 ); entreat His favor and grace.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13121"/><div sID="gen24680" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13121"/><hi type="bold">22. many ... strong nations ... in Jerusalem--</hi>In contrast to the few and weak Jews now building the temple and city, then such shall be their influence that many and strong nations shall come to worship Jehovah their God in Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.3">Is 60:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.66.23">66:23</reference>). <div eID="gen24680" type="x-p"/>

entries.reader_content_plain: 22. many ... strong nations ... in Jerusalem-- In contrast to the few and weak Jews now building the temple and city, then such shall be their influence that many and strong nations shall come to worship Jehovah their God in Jerusalem ( Is 60:3 ; 66:23 ).

Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.3.6">Is 3:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.4.1">4:1</reference>, on a different occasion. The Gentiles shall eagerly seek to share the religious privileges of the Jew. The skirt with a fringe and blue ribbon upon it (<reference osisRef="Num.15.38">Nu 15:38</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.22.12">De 22:12</reference>) was a distinguishing badge of a Jew.<div eID="gen24683" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24684" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">God is with you--</hi>the effect produced on unbelievers in entering the assemblies of the Church (<reference osisRef="1Cor.14.25">1Co 14:25</reference>). But primarily, that produced on the nations in witnessing the deliverance of the Jews by Cyrus.
